newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish higher.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended up slightly in light trading, buoyed by bullish momentum but held back by pre-FOMC jitters.

The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Tuesday and many analysts and traders expect policy makers to raise the fed funds rate at least 25 basis points. Anticipation of a Fed rate hike has kept a lid on debt futures, stemming gains in stock indices as well.
Bullish technical momentum kept Dec S&Ps in positive territory heading into the weekend, but the contract was unable to challenge its 695.00 contract high.

"I don't see us making new contract high unless we have a reason to, some sort of data or something to push us through," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "There just hasn't been much going on," he added.
The trading pit was thin ahead of Monday's Yom Kippur holiday, with some participants already gone for the holiday weekend after September's expiration on Thursday.
September settled early Friday at 684.70, up from 684.05 on the close Thursday.
"The Friday after expiration can be pretty quiet," an S&P trader said.
"The Sep did go off well and that did give us a lift," another trader said.
Still, overall action was deemed range-bound.
"I think we just have a few more longs piling on the market on pretty low volume," a trader said.
One Wall Street firm was a scale-down buyer in December on small dips in afternoon trading.
The religious holiday on Monday and nervousness before the FOMC on Tuesday could spell lethargic action on Monday also, traders said.
December S&P 500 ended up 2.05 points to 691.90, Value Lines rose 1.55 to 638.90, Midcap 400s rose 0.05 to 240.60, NYSE Composite rose 0.85 points to 367.60, and Nikkei 225 fell 145.0 to 21,140.0.
